c.tagline: Sri Lanka's east-coast harbour city of clifftop temples and calm blue beaches.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis are rare; PickMe and Uber operate but with limited coverage in Trincomalee. Most short trips are by three-wheeler (tuk-tuk) - agree the fare before setting off or ask the driver to use the PickMe app meter.

emergency.note: 119/118 reach the police; 110 is fire and rescue, and 1990 is the free nationwide Suwa Seriya ambulance service.

avoid.reason: Avoid isolated stretches of Uppuveli and Nilaveli beaches after dark and expect persistent touts around the bus stand and temple.

hood_desc: The compact city centre on a harbour peninsula, crowned by Fort Frederick and the clifftop Koneswaram Temple on Swami Rock; the practical base for markets, transport, and sights.
A relaxed beach village about 6 km north of town with a long sandy bay, guesthouses, and seafood cafes; the most popular base for beach-goers and backpackers.
A quieter stretch of wide white-sand beach roughly 16 km north, home to the area's resorts and the jumping-off point for snorkeling and diving at Pigeon Island National Park.
A small sheltered bay and promenade right by the town centre, popular with locals at sunset and lined with a few guesthouses; convenient and central.
A residential area around the inner harbour and Trincomalee's China Bay airport, near the naval base and the scenic Marble Beach; practical rather than touristy.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; avoid tap water and ice of unknown origin.

sys.n: Sri Lanka Transport Board (SLTB) & private buses

transit.pay: Bus fares are paid in cash to the conductor in small rupee notes; train tickets are bought at the station counter. There is no rechargeable transit card. Within town and to the northern beaches, hired three-wheelers (tuk-tuks) are the usual way to get around - agree the fare first or use the PickMe app.
transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5am-8pm with sparse evening service, and the trains to and from Colombo and the eastern line run limited daily schedules. After dark, tuk-tuks and ride apps are the norm.
transit.note: Trincomalee has no metro or tram; buses, tuk-tuks, and a limited rail line are the transport options, and a hired tuk-tuk or car with driver is the easiest way to reach Uppuveli, Nilaveli, and Pigeon Island.

train: Sri Lanka Railways - Trincomalee line (via Gal Oya junction to Colombo)

car.idp: Required (with a temporary Sri Lankan permit)

transit.m: Tuk-tuk to town or Uppuveli (25-35 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; a 10% service charge is often added at hotels and restaurants, and rounding up or leaving small change for good service is appreciated.
